To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) We collected a new dataset of annotator rationales for a sentiment classification task; 2) We developed two methods, discriminative and generative, for using these rationales to obtain significant accuracy gains on the sentiment classification task.

(1) annotator rationales are a useful and novel form of annotation, (2) they can be used to improve text categorization accuracy, (3) they can be collected more quickly than annotations alone, and (4) they could be useful in other machine learning settings.

(1) we can improve classification accuracy by training a machine learning algorithm using rationales that human annotators provide to explain their annotations; (2) we can reduce the cost of annotating data by having human annotators provide rationales instead of additional examples; and (3) we can use the rationales to train generative models for classification, which may be more useful for other kinds of tasks.
